title: Ops Signal Pocket Deck - Rapid Seller Triage (Draft)
content:
Slide 1 - Why this exists
- One‑pager pocket deck for sellers and SEs to triage inference incidents live during pilot/conversation.
- Problem: sellers hit runtime/perf objections, need a single fast script + playbook, not a full runbook.
- Goal: 90s confidence script + 5 rapid mitigations to keep pilot breathing.

Slide 2 - Quick 90s opener (talk track)
- "If latency or quality is worrying you, here's our 90s plan: check the SLA bucket, run a quick sample, and we can flip to a lower-cost fallback that keeps throughput while we debug."
- Purpose: reassure, buy time, preserve demo flow.
- Speaker note: use customer metric (p95 target / current) when possible.

Slide 3 - Fast diagnostic checklist (do in order)
- 1) Confirm endpoint: model name + version + region. (Ask: which route are you on?)
- 2) Validate sample: reproduce with a small representative prompt (3–5 secs).
- 3) Check token budget and request size (long context -> burst latency).
- 4) Look at error pattern: 5xx vs timeouts vs quality drift.
- 5) If throughput problem, ask about concurrency and batching settings.

Slide 4 - Rapid mitigations (playbook)
- Mitigation A: Swap to compat model variant (e.g., llama-2-q8 -> llama-2-q4f16). Immediate: lower latency, may change quality slightly.
- Mitigation B: Enable prefix cache (customer pilot buckets) for repeated prompts.
- Mitigation C: Shorten max_tokens and force temperature 0.0 for deterministic speed.
- Mitigation D: Route to Dedicated capacity or different region (if latency spikes are infra-related).
- Mitigation E: Fall back to non-streaming mode when streaming overhead causing jitter.

Slide 5 - Quick fallback script (copyable)
- "Let's temporarily route the integration to model X-compat for the rest of the session and I'll spin up a short performance test. If throughput looks good, we'll roll a canary and come back with a quantified tradeoff."
- When to use: demo fail, pilot performance concern, procurement asks for latency proof.

Slide 6 - Customer questions & rebuttals (fast hits)
- Q: "Why is this slower than your benchmark?" -> A: "Benchmarks are measured on our curated dataset; your live prompt size and concurrency change the profile. Let's run a fast local sample."
- Q: "Can you guarantee 50ms?" -> A: "We tier latency with SLOs; for <50ms we point to Dedicated configs — we can propose a starter commit to prove it."
- Q: "Will fallbacks change outputs?" -> A: "Minor changes possible; we include regression checks and can preserve critical prompts via canary rollout."

Slide 7 - Pilot adjustment checklist (next 24 hours)
- Record: failing prompts, p95 latency, concurrency, model version.
- Action: flip fallback for session, schedule canary with ops, add ~5 representative prompts to regression set.
- Deliverable: within 24h provide a short note with observed numbers + recommended route.

Slide 8 - SE playbook snippets (what to capture)
- Capture a 10‑token sample + full prompt.
- Note whether streaming was used and which SDK.
- Save request ids and timestamps for support handoff.
- Tag customer in shared Slack channel: #pilot-ops with subject: "Pilot: latency incident — attach ids".

Slide 9 - Tradeoff cheat sheet (one line each)
- Quantization: +cost down, +latency down, -rare quality delta.
- Batching: +throughput up, +p95 variance; good when concurrency > X.
- Prefix cache: huge wins for repetitive prompts, 0 config cost but requires warm runs.
- Dedicated: best p95 predictability, commit required.

Slide 10 - Proposed escalation ladder
- Level 0: Seller/SE uses this deck + fallback (no tickets).
- Level 1: Ops engineer (triage channel) — collect logs, canary config.
- Level 2: SRE/Eng — infra incident, hotfix, model rollback.

Slide 11 - Example play (real mini-case)
- Customer: legal doc summarization pilot, p95 spiking to 3s during multi-file prompts.
- Quick fix: temporary model variant + enable prefix cache for repeated doc headers -> p95 dropped to 700ms.
- Follow up: add 6 prompts to regression, run quality A/B on 2k tokens.

Slide 12 - Checklist for sending to engineering
- Include: request ids, sample prompt, model+variant, observed p95 and throughput, selected mitigation attempted.
- Template subject line: "Pilot triage: <customer> — p95 XXms — attempted swap to <variant> — attach ids"

Slide 13 - Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Need a short mapping of "compat variants" by model family (separate doc).
- Add 1‑pager on quantization delta examples for SE reference.
- Integrate a tiny runnable script sellers can run locally (curl + prompt).

Slide 14 - Appendix: quick runnable curl (example)
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -d '{"model":"model-x:compat","input":"<short prompt>","max_tokens":40}'
- Speaker note: only for quick reproduction in customer session, not for benchmarking.

Slide 15 - Closing notes and release plan
- Current doc status: draft — want feedback from 3 SEs and 1 ops engineer.
- Target: ship as "seller-ops-pocket-v0.1" and link into enablement hub.
- Questions for review: is fallback wording convincing? do sellers have curl comfort?

---
Author notes (informal):
- Keep language lightweight, sellers need a script not an RFC.
- Avoid heavy appendices in the main deck; link out to deeper artifacts.
- Will iterate based on pilot outcomes; expected 2–3 more rounds before wide roll.
